question.prompt: A cone-shaped mountain has its base on the ocean floor and has a height of \(8000\) feet. The top \(\tfrac{1}{8}\) of the volume of the mountain is above water. What is the depth of the ocean at the base of the mountain, in feet?

solutions.explanation:
The exposed tip is a smaller cone similar to the entire mountain, so its volume fraction is the cube of its height fraction. We can see why by comparing the cone-volume formulas.

Let \(h\), with \(0<h<8000\), be the height above water. Let \(r>0\) be the radius at the waterline and \(R>0\) the full base radius. In a cross-section through the axis, the waterline is parallel to the base. The small and large triangles are therefore similar, giving
\[
\frac{r}{R}=\frac{h}{8000}.
\]
Using the cone-volume formula \(V=\tfrac13\pi r^2h\), the ratio of exposed volume to total volume is
\[
\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^2\frac{h}{8000}
=\left(\frac{h}{8000}\right)^3.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\left(\frac{h}{8000}\right)^3=\frac18
=\left(\frac12\right)^3,
\]
so \(h=4000\). The ocean depth is the remaining height, \(8000-4000=\boxed{4000}\) feet, choice A.
solutions.title: Convert volume ratio to height ratio
